turn_text: So now that you have held several hearings, what kinds of changes do we need to make either an antitrust policy or antitrust enforcement?

Well, I think it's important to acknowledge that the situation we find ourselves in with respect to the digital platforms is partly a result of the lack of good antitrust enforcement, robust enforcement by both Democratic and Republican administrations. I think there was a sense that these are great American companies providing really interesting services and a lot of excitement in people's attitude was sort of let them flourish, leave them alone. Not fully appreciating at the time what their market dominance would produce and what the implications were for the kind of market share that they had. I think the Europeans were ahead of us in sort of understanding that. So I think really good strong antitrust enforcement is critical. That means making certain that the antitrust laws are capable of responding to the competition challenges in the 21st century. I mean, our interest laws were written at the turn of the last century in response to the railroad and oil monopolies. This is quite a different economy. So one of the things that we're looking at during the course of this investigation is do we have to modernize or update antitrust statutes to reflect the challenges that the lack of competition in the digital marketplace presents? are antitrust agencies resource properly so that they can vigorously enforce competition policy? And are they staffed and led by people who are sufficiently enthusiastic and creative to use the existing antitrust laws in a way that really promotes competition? But one of the things the investigation is looking at and what we expect to do when we complete the report is put together a menu of options for policymakers, including my colleagues, on the ways that we can bring more competition into this digital marketplace. That can range from some really obvious things like requiring portability and interoperability so people can move from one platform to another easily without friction that will help create more opportunities for new entrants in the marketplace. All the way to things like having sort of a blast eagle for the internet that is not allowing someone to be both a seller of goods and services and a person who controls the marketplace that can be one or the other. You can't set all the rules, control the marketplace, and also sell on it. in the way that Amazon does, for example. So I think we'll have a whole menu of ideas. This effort has been very bipartisan. We may not have bipartisan agreement on every single recommendation, but the purpose of the investigation is to thoroughly understand the marketplace and then develop a set of solutions, both in terms of statutory changes and propose new regulations to bring competition back into the space.

turn_text: So much of antitrust law has been based on the consumer welfare standard. In order to bring antitrust actions, there has to be discernible harm to consumers.
